name: Inverness Clubhouse
desc: 2072 Azalea Dr, the heart of the neighborhood.
detail: The gathering room and point of reference for everything else.
cardDesc: 2072 Azalea Drive, Roswell, GA 30075. The neighborhood's gathering room serves as the point of reference for everything else.

name: Chattahoochee Nature Center
desc: 127 acres of forest, wetland, and river habitat with trails, exhibits, and a wildlife clinic.
detail: Metro Atlanta's nature destination, with the mission to connect people with nature.
cardDesc: Metro Atlanta's nature destination, set on 127 acres of forest, wetland, and river habitat along the Chattahoochee River. The center has guided trails, interactive exhibits, environmental education programs, and an on-site wildlife clinic. Special events include the Butterfly Encounter, Halloween Hikes, and the annual Holiday Market.

name: Roswell Riverwalk Boardwalk and Trail
desc: A scenic boardwalk and paved multi-use trail along the Chattahoochee.
detail: Begins at the dam at Morgan Falls Park, follows the river, and extends eastward to connect with the Vickery Creek Trail and beyond.
cardDesc: A scenic boardwalk and paved riverside trail beginning at Morgan Falls Park dam. The path winds alongside the Chattahoochee and runs 3+ miles eastward past the Vickery Creek Trail, an easy route for walking, running, or cycling.

name: Roswell Town Square
desc: The 1839 square, with the original bandstand.
detail: Mill workers cottages and Barrington Hall across the street.
cardDesc: Laid out in 1839 by Roswell King, the square features the original bandstand, the founding cottages, and Barrington Hall across the street.

name: Downtown Roswell
desc: Restaurants, shops, and galleries along Canton Street.
detail: The monthly Alive After Five street festival, April through October.
cardDesc: Canton Street offers restaurants, galleries, and the monthly Alive After Five street festival running from April through October.

name: Azalea Park
desc: A wooded playground and picnic area directly on the Chattahoochee River.
detail: Shaded picnic tables, natural playground, and riverfront trails for a peaceful escape.
cardDesc: A shaded, riverfront playground and picnic area with wooded trails along the Chattahoochee — a peaceful spot for families and nature lovers alike.

name: Azalea Boat Launch
desc: River access for kayaks, canoes, and fishing along the Chattahoochee.
detail: A popular put-in and take-out spot for paddlers exploring the National Recreation Area.
cardDesc: A concrete boat launch and parking area for kayaks, canoes, and fishing. This popular access point serves paddlers exploring the Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area.

name: Riverside Park
desc: A sprawling park with playgrounds, spraygrounds, and an amphitheater.
detail: Hosts summer concerts, movie nights, and community festivals for the whole family.
cardDesc: A sprawling riverfront park with a massive playground, spraygrounds, and an outdoor amphitheater. The park hosts summer concerts, movie nights, and community festivals throughout the season.

name: Riverside Recreation Area
desc: Outdoor volleyball courts and fitness trails along the river.
detail: Open-air courts and exercise stations with scenic Chattahoochee River views.
cardDesc: Open-air volleyball courts and outdoor fitness stations set along the riverbank provide a scenic spot for active recreation with Chattahoochee River views.

name: Old Mill Park & Vickery Creek
desc: The mill ruins, the 1853 machine shop, and the covered bridge on Vickery Creek.
detail: Where Roswell's industrial past meets the National Recreation Area's trails.
cardDesc: Below the 1839 town square, Vickery Creek runs through the ruins of the mill that built Roswell. The remains of the 1853 machine shop, the dam, and the covered bridge stand beside the trailhead, where the Vickery Creek Trail begins its miles of riverside hiking through the National Recreation Area.

name: The Southern Trilogy
desc: Barrington Hall, Bulloch Hall, and Smith Plantation — the three founding homes, open to the public.
detail: Bulloch Hall is where Theodore Roosevelt's parents were married in 1853.
cardDesc: Three of Roswell's founding homes — Barrington Hall, Bulloch Hall, and Smith Plantation — are preserved and open for tours. Bulloch Hall, where Martha Bulloch married Theodore Roosevelt Sr. in 1853, was the childhood home of President Theodore Roosevelt's mother.

name: North Fulton Hospital
desc: Full-service hospital on Hospital Boulevard near GA 400.
detail: Emergency care and a full range of medical services, minutes north of Inverness.
cardDesc: A full-service community hospital with emergency care and a broad range of medical services, located off Alpharetta Highway near GA 400. Children's Healthcare of Atlanta at Scottish Rite is roughly seven miles south for pediatric care.

name: Kroger
desc: Full-service grocery at 900 Marietta Hwy, minutes from the neighborhood entrance.
detail: The everyday errand run — groceries and more, close enough to walk.
cardDesc: A full-service Kroger at 900 Marietta Highway, serving the south Roswell area. At 0.4 miles from the clubhouse, it's close enough to walk for everyday errands — groceries, household essentials, and pharmacy stops without a second thought.
